text:
raj: heads-up — since the eu-west deploy we're seeing intermittent DNS failures from edge GPU nodes to internal k8s svc names. apps get NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL for short bursts

maria: which names? full fqdn examples?

raj: e.g. `trainer-service.default.svc.cluster.local` sometimes resolves, sometimes NXDOMAIN. Happens for a subset of nodes in the edge pool only (eu-west-1a/b).

kevin: can you paste a `dig +short` and the node's /etc/resolv.conf?

raj: here's dig from one affected node:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.13-Ubuntu <<>> trainer-service.default.svc.cluster.local +short +time=3
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
and the resolv.conf:
```
search eu.prod.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 169.254.169.253
options ndots:5 timeout:2 attempts:3 rotate
```

santiago: that nameserver IP is our node-local stub (dnsmasq -> coredns). Does the node-local pod log show anything?

raj: checked node-local logs, no obvious errors. kube-dns/coredns in cluster shows a few "servfail" spikes around the same timestamps.

maria: could be searchpath expansion + ndots causing long queries that get truncated or trigger different upstream behavior. Any EDNS size/UDP truncation in logs?

kevin: also consider source-port reuse from NAT egress. Edge nodes go through a NAT gateway for egress lookup of cross-vpc names; if UDP responses map to wrong socket it looks like random failures. Has anyone seen high conntrack churn?

raj: conntrack on the NAT is normal but we did push a kernel update yesterday to the edge nodes around same time.

ops-bot: Incident note: 1993456789 - intermittent DNS failures in eu-west edge pool. Pager duty routed to eng-infra.

santiago: quick checks: 1) try `systemd-resolve --flush-caches` on node-local, 2) temporarily set `options ndots:1` in resolv.conf symlink to avoid search-first expansion, 3) enable TCP fallback for dig/tests (`+tcp`) to see if UDP truncation.

raj: did `systemd-resolve --flush-caches`, still saw a couple of failures. Flipping ndots to 1 reduced failures a lot on one node (ran for 10m without NXDOMAIN), but we can't change cluster-wide yet.

kevin: that points to search expansion being the multiplier. If the expanded name exceeds 255 bytes or triggers upstream rules it can fail. Another angle: dnsmasq has a cache TTL mismatch with coredns leading to stale negative caching — check `negative_ttl` settings.

maria: can we repro locally by crafting long searchpath? run: `resolvectl query trainer-service.default.svc.cluster.local --tries=3` and `dig trainer-service +search` to see exact wire queries. Also collect tcpdump on port 53 for a failing window.

raj: started tcpdump on node-local, captured a few failure windows. Observed repeated queries for the expanded name and then a truncated UDP packet (TC bit set) followed by no TCP retry from the resolver. The node-local stub (dnsmasq) seems to drop the TCP fallback.

santiago: if dnsmasq is configured not to do TCP or systemd-resolved isn't configured to fall back, that explains intermittent NXDOMAIN. We changed dnsmasq config to disable TCP in a previous hardening PR to avoid long-lived tcp sockets on edge.

kevin: OK, plan: 1) revert the dnsmasq TCP disable on edge node-local pods (hotfix), 2) set a shorter search path for edge nodes (remove cluster.long suffix), 3) add a short-term iptables rule to force DNS traffic to use a dedicated egress IP to reduce source-port collisions. Can we do 1) now?

raj: rolling dnsmasq config revert to 10% of the edge pool now. Will report after 5 mins.

(5m later)

raj: rolled to 30% — nodes in that cohort show almost zero NXDOMAINs for 15m.

maria: good sign. For long-term: we should 1) make node-local respect TCP fallback, 2) tune ndots for edge workloads that do cross-namespace lookups more often, 3) add monitoring for DNS TC flags and TCP fallbacks in the console.

santiago: also file a regression with the kernel update + conntrack churn as follow-up, but main root cause appears to be TCP fallback disabled in node-local dns proxy combined with searchpath-expansion creating UDP truncation. Two factors compounding.

kevin: can someone open a CHORE and include tcpdump sample, dnsmasq config diff, and the ndots experiment? I'll add the rollout and SLA note.

raj: creating CHORE-EDGE-764 with attachments now. tagging @maria for console metrics.
